summary: Book is running hot: portfolio beta ~3.5 vs a 'balanced' stated profile, with three positions (RKLB, QQQ, APLD) breaching the 15% single-name comfort line and most holdings showing RSI in the high 60s/low 70s. The setup has worked — large unrealized gains across RKLB (+63%), APLD (+54%), ONDS (+110%) — but you are now structurally long high-beta AI/space/compute at extended prices with zero cash. The right move is risk reduction into strength, not new adds.

insights.headline: Parabolic winner, oversized at 29% — trim to respect risk limits
insights.detail: +242% in 6 months, RSI 71, 89% annualized vol, beta 2.31, and nearly a third of the book. Stored thesis itself flags 25–40% mean-reversion as normal behavior for this name. Blue Origin/New Glenn explosion headline is a reminder of single-launch tail risk.

suggested_action.thesis: Position has compounded into a 29% weight in a 3.5-beta book at RSI 71 after a 242% run. Trimming back toward the 15% comfort cap locks in gains and lowers correlated drawdown risk without abandoning the Neutron/Electron thesis.
suggested_action.catalyst: Any launch slip, equity raise, or space-sector rotation can produce a 25–40% drawdown given vol; trimming now is risk management, not a call on the company.
suggested_action.risks: Stock keeps melting up post-trim and you underparticipate; tax drag on a +63% unrealized gain.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: Stated max single-position is 15%; balanced risk appetite is incompatible with a 29% weight in an 89%-vol name.

insights.headline: Overweight at 26% and stacks the same tech factor you already own in singles
insights.detail: RSI 68, +21% 3m, above both MAs. Trend intact but it's not diversifying — it overlaps APLD/ONDS/RKLB AI-adjacent exposure and is above your 15% cap.

suggested_action.thesis: QQQ is a fine core, but at 26% it's both over the position cap and redundant with existing tech singles. Trim a few points and redeploy into lower-beta ballast (e.g., VOO) to actually reduce factor risk.
suggested_action.catalyst: AI capex disappointment or rate re-acceleration would hit QQQ and your single names together; trimming reduces correlated drawdown.
suggested_action.risks: Nasdaq continues to lead and the trim underperforms a held position; minor tax friction.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: Brings position back under the 15% comfort line and reduces stacked tech beta in an already 3.5-beta book.

insights.headline: Over the 15% cap on a 5.7-beta, 114%-vol name — take some off
insights.detail: 18% weight, beta 5.70, vol 114%, +90% 6m. Real catalyst (the $7.5B hyperscaler lease) is in the price; single-customer concentration and likely financing dilution are live risks.

suggested_action.thesis: The fundamental catalyst already triggered the re-rate. At 5.7 beta and 114% vol, a 30–40% give-back on no company-specific news is routine. Trim back under 15% to protect the +54% gain.
suggested_action.catalyst: Equity raise to fund campus capex, hyperscaler/AI sentiment cooling, or simple mechanical mean reversion.
suggested_action.risks: More hyperscaler deals or upside guidance push it higher post-trim.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: Respects the 15% single-position cap on the highest-beta name in the book.

insights.headline: The only real ballast — underweight relative to where this book needs to be
insights.detail: Beta ~1, vol 12%, only 10.6% of book. This is the position that actually lowers your 3.5 portfolio beta. RSI 69 is extended but trend is clean.

suggested_action.thesis: Funding VOO from RKLB/QQQ/APLD trims mechanically lowers portfolio beta and diversifies away from the AI/space/compute factor you're tripled-up on.
suggested_action.catalyst: Not a momentum trade — purpose is structural risk reduction. Stagger adds to avoid RSI 69 entry.
suggested_action.risks: VOO itself is at highs; near-term 5–10% pullback possible. Internal mega-cap tech weighting reduces true diversification benefit.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: Balanced risk profile + medium horizon argues for a meaningful index core, which the current book lacks.

insights.headline: Hot momentum but not yet euphoric; size is reasonable
insights.detail: +40% 1m, RSI 52, beta 4.18, vol 101%, 8.8% weight. Position size is fine; the name is just inherently volatile and tied to both bitcoin and AI capex narratives.

insights.headline: Mid-recovery setup, below 200d MA — hold, don't add
insights.detail: +13% 1m, RSI 70, above 50d but still below 200d. Trend change not yet confirmed. 5.5% weight is appropriately sized for the uncertainty.

suggested_action.thesis: Recovery is real but unconfirmed by the 200d MA. Insider buying and stablecoin/platform momentum are constructive, but RSI 70 makes adding here a chase.
suggested_action.catalyst: Next earnings print validating Galileo/platform revenue acceleration; reclaim of 200d MA on volume.
suggested_action.risks: Credit deterioration in personal loans; valuation compression at 40x P/E if growth stalls.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: Reasonable size, asymmetric setup — holding lets the thesis prove itself without adding to high-beta exposure.

insights.headline: Lottery ticket working — let it run, do not add
insights.detail: +110% unrealized on a 2.2% weight. RSI 71, vol 126%, 147x P/E, story-driven on Pentagon drone funding rumors. Size is the only reason this is tolerable.

suggested_action.thesis: Small enough position that a 50% drawdown costs ~1% of book, while continued narrative momentum preserves upside optionality. Adding would convert a controlled bet into a real risk.
suggested_action.catalyst: Conversion of Pentagon funding talk into an actual contract; further order announcements.
suggested_action.risks: 'No deal' clarification, dilutive raise into the spike, momentum exhaustion — 30–50% drawdowns are routine at 126% vol.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: Position sizing is doing the risk management; leave it alone.

insights.headline: Tiny stub on a parabolic thematic — either size up intentionally or close
insights.detail: 0.3% weight is too small to matter after a +61% 1m move; RSI 67, vol 72%. Either a real thesis position or noise on the statement.

suggested_action.thesis: At 0.3% it can't move the needle and adds line-item clutter on a stretched thematic ETF. Cleaner to redeploy into VOO ballast or, if you want memory exposure, own MU directly.
suggested_action.catalyst: Memory cycles top violently; entering after a 60% move is paying peak premium.
suggested_action.risks: Memory super-cycle continues and DRAM keeps ripping — but at 0.3% the opportunity cost is trivial.
suggested_action.fits_profile_because: Reduces noise; frees capital for either ballast or a properly-sized conviction position.

concentration_flags: RKLB at 29% — nearly 2x the 15% single-position comfort cap, on a 2.3-beta name with 89% vol
QQQ at 26% — over the 15% cap and factor-redundant with existing tech singles
APLD at 18% — over the 15% cap on the highest-beta name in the book (5.7)
Portfolio beta ~3.5 vs a 'balanced' stated risk appetite — structural mismatch
Zero cash — no dry powder to buy a drawdown in any of these high-vol names
Industrials + Tech + AI-infrastructure factor stacking across RKLB, APLD, IREN, ONDS, DRAM, QQQ
